description: Person prepends Logger, which defines its own speak calling `super`. prepend puts Logger *ahead* of Person in the ancestor chain, so Person.new.speak resolves to Logger#speak first, whose bare `super` (a `zsuper` node) forwards to the *next* speak in the chain -- Person's own. Typing this needs an MRO-aware `super'`/`zsuper` rule on top of the prepend-ordered ancestry -- a genuinely nontrivial dispatch-design item, but still no new Ty vocabulary: both speak methods have the same arrow_of([], an instance of String) shape as anywhere else.
